record.original_question: Let 1 = d_1 < d_2 < ... < d_tau(n) = n be the increasing sequence of positive divisors of n, and define H(n) as the sum of 1 / (d_j - d_i) over all pairs 1 <= i < j <= tau(n). Is H(n) < tau(n) for every n > 5040, equivalently for every n outside the listed exceptional set {12, 24, 60, 120, 180, 240, 360, 420, 720, 840, 1260, 1680, 2520, 5040}?

evidence.quote: Does H(n) < tau (n) hold for n > 5040?
It is conjectured in [11] (cf. also [25], problem 23, p. 200)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$, let $1 = d_1 < d_2 < \cdots < d_{\tau(n)} = n$ be the increasing sequence of all positive divisors of $n$, where $\tau(n)$ denotes the number of divisors of $n$. Define
$$H(n) = \sum_{1 \le i < j \le \tau(n)} \frac{1}{d_j - d_i}.$$
Prove or disprove: for every integer $n > 5040$, one has $H(n) < \tau(n)$. Equivalently, show that the only positive integers $n$ for which $H(n) \ge \tau(n)$ are precisely the elements of the finite set
$$\{12, 24, 60, 120, 180, 240, 360, 420, 720, 840, 1260, 1680, 2520, 5040\}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture concerns a specific inequality between the divisor-gap harmonic sum H(n) and τ(n). Related work by T. Tao (2025) addresses a different (but related) Erdős conjecture #884 on sums of reciprocals of divisor gaps, and conditionally disproves it under the prime tuples conjecture. No direct resolution of the specific inequality H(n) < τ(n) for all n > 5040 was found, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the sum of reciprocals of gaps between divisors (T. Tao)
status_evidence.snippet: Theorem 1.1 (Erdős #884) ... conditionally disproves a conjecture of Erdős on divisor gaps, assuming the prime tuples conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: A related Erdős conjecture about sums over divisor gaps has only recently received (conditional) progress; the specific H(n) < τ(n) inequality is not addressed.
